proposals.impact: remove intro-screen drop-off blocking all quiz starts
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, two sessions reached the quiz intro screen and neither progressed. starts = 0, completions = 0, furthest_step_distribution shows both sessions stalled at intro_load. The quiz is receiving traffic from two distinct sources (direct and the Netlify subdomain) but something on the intro screen is killing intent before a single question is answered. This is the entire top of the funnel.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is doing too much work or making too big an ask before the visitor has any reason to trust the process. The fix: strip the intro to one grounded sentence of context, one line of what the quiz actually does in plain terms, and a single button. Remove any multi-step preamble, credential blocks, or anything that resembles a landing page within a landing page. Every extra element at this stage costs starts. The goal is to get the visitor to question one: once they answer one question, completion rates rise sharply across most short quiz formats. Audit also whether the "Start" button is firing correctly in production — the Quiz Events workflow failed twice today (06:02 and 10:07), which may mean event tracking errors are a symptom of a broader JS initialisation fault that could itself be blocking the start interaction.
proposals.new_text:
Most people who earn well still feel behind with money. This quiz identifies which thinking pattern is driving that — based on established research into how people relate to financial decisions.

Five minutes. No email required to begin.

proposals.impact: replicate 66% open rate pattern across lower-performing sequences
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Avoidance is at 52.63% across 19 sends. Money Worship is at 37.5% across 16 sends — nearly 30 percentage points below Money Vigilance. These are three sequences running in the same product, to the same ICP, presumably with similar send cadence. The subject line and preview text of the Money Vigilance sequence are doing something the Worship sequence is not.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject line and preview text from email one of the Money Vigilance sequence and apply the same structural logic (not copy-paste, but same approach: specific, self-referential, no resolution promised) to the subject line of email one in the Money Worship sequence. A 29-point open rate gap between sequences for the same audience is almost always a subject line problem, not a content problem. The content never gets read if the open does not happen. This is a single line change in one file with no deliverability risk.
proposals.new_text: subject: "You know money matters. So why does wanting more of it feel embarrassing?"

proposals.impact: convert existing blog traffic into quiz starts
proposals.observation: The blog post "Why do I feel like everyone my age has money figured out except me?" was committed and published today (sha 9a414ff). It targets the exact ICP age range (25-35, comparison anxiety, earning well but not building). There is no evidence in the data of a quiz CTA inside the post body. The quiz is the primary conversion mechanism for the funnel. Publishing a high-relevance post without a route into the quiz leaves the traffic with nowhere to go.
proposals.proposal: Add a single inline CTA block roughly two-thirds of the way through the post body, after the section where the comparison anxiety theme peaks and before any resolution framing. Position matters: too early feels like a grab, too late misses the emotional activation window. The CTA should name the specific thing the quiz does, in plain language, without promising a transformation.
proposals.new_text:
If that comparison feeling is familiar, it tends to come from a specific pattern in how you think about money — not a character flaw, not laziness. Joel built a short quiz that identifies which pattern fits you, based on your actual answers rather than a general type.

Take the quiz (five minutes)
